land.text: the Jaffna peninsula, the islands off it, Mannar Island and the Vanni: the lands the Portuguese conquest page lists for the kingdom

successors.note: 'In 1619, a land expedition by Phillippe de Oliveira and his army of 5000 was able to defeat Cankili' (Portuguese conquest page); the Jaffna page puts the end of the kingdom's independent existence in 1619. Cliopatria's Jaffna row ends in 1594 and its Portuguese Ceylon outline already holds the kingdom's 37 cells in 1595-1618 (hand-off to sa-06).

capitals.name: Nallur (Jaffna)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Nallur'; Ibn Battuta's 1344 account gives 'two capitals: one in Nallur in the north and the other in Puttalam in the west' during the pearling season. Nallur is not in the gazetteer; the coordinates are the gazetteer's Jaffna town, in which Nallur lies. No page gives years for the seat.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1258-1313: Cliopatria starts the row in 1314, but the lead has the kingdom 'a tribute-paying feudatory of the Pandyan Empire in modern South India in 1258', 'on the Jaffna Peninsula', and the infobox has 'Pandyas installed Aryacakravarti: 1277' (body: 1262). The land is the peninsula, 8 cells (about 2,500 km2). The Vannimai regions 'just south of the Jaffna peninsula and in the eastern Trincomalee district usually paid an annual tribute' (undated) and are not drawn before 1314.

correction.text: the Jaffna peninsula, the core of the kingdom

keyframe_review.note: 22,777 km2 (76 cells) for 1314-1351: the peninsula, the Vanni, Trincomalee, Mannar and Puttalam country, with 26 Anuradhapura and 5 Puttalam cells. It fits the page's 'Ibn Battuta's 1344 account says the kingdom had two capitals: one in Nallur in the north and the other in Puttalam in the west' and the Vanni 'feudatories' paying tribute; the page dates no conquest of the plains, and the independence from the Pandyas is 1323 on the infobox. The page gives no area to compare.

Holds for 1352-1449 and 1467-1587 only (Cliopatria 11,785 km2, 37 cells: the Northern Province and Trincomalee; the Portuguese conquest page's lands are 'the Jaffna Peninsula, the islands off Jaffna and the Island of Mannar' and the Vanni and Vannimai chieftaincies, the modern Northern Province and the northern half of the Eastern Province). The shape is right in substance; the years are not: the kingdom 'briefly los[t] its independence under the Kotte kingdom from 1450 to 1467', so there is no kingdom in 1450-1466 (ledger loss and gain, Ceylon takes the land). Mannar Island, taken by the Portuguese in 1560, is under one cell and is left in the outline.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1352 outline unchanged, absent for 1450-1466

keyframe_review.note: Holds for 1588-1594 (Cliopatria 11,785 km2, the same outline as 1352): the page has the kingdom after 1591 under 'Ethirimanna Cinkam' as 'nominally a client' of the Portuguese, with a tribute of ten elephants by 1582, and no loss of land. The outline is unchanged; the row simply stops in 1594 while the kingdom lasts to 1619 (new keyframe 1595).

New keyframe 1595-1619: the same 37-cell outline, 11,785 km2. Cliopatria has no Jaffna row after 1594 and draws these cells in its Portuguese Ceylon row for 1595-1618; the page has no Portuguese annexation before 1619 ('The page gives no specific annexation date'; the Jaffna page: 'the kingdom's independent existence to an end in 1619'), and the king installed in 1591 is 'nominally a client'.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1588 outline, held to 1619 as a nominal client of the Portuguese from 1591

ledger.note: 1258: the Jaffna kingdom enters the record. The lead has it 'a tribute-paying feudatory of the Pandyan Empire in modern South India in 1258' and 'traditionally thought to have been established after the invasion of Kalinga Magha'; the infobox starts in 1215 ('Kalinga Magha's invasion of Sri Lanka led to the fall of the Polonnaruwa kingdom') and installs the Aryacakravarti in 1277 (body 1262). 1258 is the first year the kingdom itself is dated, and the Pandya dossier's vassal event starts that year. The land is the peninsula, my reading.

region.text: the Vanni, Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, Mannar and Puttalam country of Cliopatria's 1314 outline, beyond the peninsula

ledger.note: 1314: the plains south of the peninsula join the kingdom. The page dates nothing in 1314 and gives the kingdom independent of the Pandyas in 1323; the year is Cliopatria's (its Jaffna row starts in 1314 with 22.8k km2), and the Ceylon dossier records the same loss.

region.text: Anuradhapura and Puttalam, the cells of the 1314 outline that the 1352 outline drops

ledger.note: 1352: the plains go back. Cliopatria's Jaffna row shrinks to 11.8k km2 and its Ceylon row regains Anuradhapura and Puttalam; the page dates no loss (it has Puttalam as the second capital in 1344).

1450: Kotte conquers the kingdom. 'The kingdom was overpowered by the rival Kotte kingdom around 1450', invaded 'under the orders of Parakramabahu VI' by Prince Sapumal; 'the first invasion did not succeed ... the second invasion dated to 1450 eventually was successful'; the kingdom 'briefly los[t] its independence under the Kotte kingdom from 1450 to 1467'.

1467: the kingdom is restored. 'It gained independence from kingdom of Kotte control in 1467'; infobox 'Aryacakravarti dynasty restored: 1467'; Kanakasooriya Cinkaiariyan 'and his two son's returned from Madurai with mercenaries' to reclaim the throne.

1560: the Portuguese take Mannar Island. Viceroy Dom Constantino de Bragança's first expedition 'failed to subdue the kingdom but captured Mannar Island' (the Jaffna page: 'wrested Mannar Island from it'). Year from the pages; the island is under one cell, my reading of its place.

region.text: the Jaffna kingdom, passing to the Portuguese

ledger.note: 1619: the kingdom ends. 'In 1619, a land expedition by Phillippe de Oliveira and his army of 5000 was able to defeat Cankili' (Cankili II became a prisoner and was later hanged); the Jaffna page: 'the kingdom's independent existence to an end in 1619'. The Portuguese infobox runs 1560-1621; the page gives 'By June 1619' and no annexation date.

wars.name: Kotte-Jaffna war
wars.outcome: Prince Sapumal's second invasion in 1450 took the kingdom for Kotte after a failed first attempt; the dynasty came back in 1467 with mercenaries from Madurai.
wars.note: The page dates the first invasion nowhere. The Tenkasi inscription 'is dated between 1449-50 and 1453-54' and the page links it to a Pandyan victory over Kotte; no land is named.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna kingdom
wars.outcome: 1560: Mannar Island taken, the kingdom not subdued. 1591: King Puvirasa Pandaram killed and Ethirimanna Cinkam installed as a nominal client. 1619: the capital taken and Cankili II captured; the kingdom fell.
wars.note: Infobox 'Date: 1560-1621'. The Portuguese page's infobox lists no territorial change; Kandyan attacks were repulsed.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary. The peninsula is certain; the Vanni and Trincomalee edges and the 1314 extension to Anuradhapura and Puttalam are Cliopatria's, undated by any page.

notes: Jaffna kingdom: three Cliopatria shapes (1314-1594) reviewed against the Jaffna kingdom and Portuguese conquest pages (the budget). Start: 1258, the first year the kingdom itself is dated (a Pandyan feudatory); the infobox start is 1215 (Kalinga Magha's invasion) and the Aryacakravarti installation is 1262 in the body and 1277 in the infobox; independence 1323 on the infobox, 'early 14th century' in the body. A gap-filler may back-date the start to 1215 if the Kalinga Magha line is read as the kingdom's. Cliopatria starts in 1314. End: 1619 (Portuguese page and Jaffna page; the Portuguese infobox runs 1560-1621). Cliopatria's Jaffna row ends in 1594 and its Portuguese Ceylon row draws all 37 Jaffna cells in 1595-1618 and only 5 from 1619, the reverse of the pages. The pages do not support: a conquest of the plains in 1314 or their loss in 1352 (both Cliopatria's years, ledger confidence 1); an area (none on either page). Vassalage is recorded by the suzerains: the Pandya dossier already has vassal_start 1258 and vassal_end 1323; the Jaffna page has the kingdom 'a vassal of the Vijayanagara Empire in 1440's' (Vijayanagara dossier, and Cliopatria's relation row 1385-1501); the Portuguese page has the king 'nominally a client' after 1591 and a tribute of ten elephants by 1582, to be recorded by portuguese-ceylon (sa-06) as vassal_start 1591 and vassal_end 1619. Not in the pages opened: Singai Nagar, Batticaloa, Chilaw, Gampola, the 1344 conquest of Gampola and the 1588 and 1594 dates. Region names missing from the gazetteer: Nallur (coordinates of Jaffna town used), Mannar Island (a 20 km circle at 79.92, 8.98 within Sri Lanka).
